mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where FEDFUNDS has declined over the prior month, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce corporate earnings expectations, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 1 month, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts and real personal consumption expenditures above their 3-month moving averages indicates robust consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where both HOUST and RSAFS are above their 3-month moving averages, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production, the S&P 500 tends to underperform as manufacturing weakness signals an impending recession, leading to negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where INDPRO falls > 0.5% in 3 months, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI reading above 3.5% signals persistent inflation that triggers aggressive monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 3.5%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls over the past month signals a strengthening labor market that supports consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where PAYEMS has increased over the prior month, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of slowing real GDP growth (quarterly GDP growth rate below 1.0%), the S&P 500 tends to experience negative forward returns as recession risks rise, over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where GDPC1 growth < 1.0% (q/q annualized), or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production and real GDP growth below 1.0% signals a deepening economic slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods where both INDPRO declines and GDPC1 growth < 1.0%, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.
